column3: note
Left edge of the journey bar (Å). 0 = auto = 1216 Å: the birth tick is the left edge (no Ly-alpha line ever lives left of it).

Right edge of the bar (Å). 9000 = DECIDED 2026-10-04 (option A): UV / visible / IR all on the bar (visible 4000–7000 Å) so the tutorial's band division and the journey share one axis. At Earth the Ly-alpha peak (~5610 Å) sits at ~76%.
Samples across the bar. The HUD draws 512; 1024 keeps narrow features from aliasing.
Steps along the journey. Uniform in ln(1+z) — every step is the same amount of stretch.
Internal cells per step (~40 km/s). Fine enough for the arrival frame to resolve forest lines like the reference figure. Bake time only; no runtime cost.
Density samples averaged into each cell.

Light-travel time of the journey in Gyr → quasar at z = 3.62 (like Q1422+2309; decided so the arrival looks like the classic forest figure). MUST MATCH UniverseJourneyTracker's first phase remainingDistanceAtStart (12070000000 ly).
Same seed = same forest every bake.
Lognormal density contrast of the intergalactic gas. Approximate — shapes texture only.
Correlation length of the density field in km/s. Approximate — shapes texture only.
tau ∝ rho^alpha with alpha = 2 − 0.7(gamma − 1) and gamma ≈ 1.6.
Quasar continuum slope F_lambda ∝ lambda^alpha (Selsing et al. 2016).
Where the continuum is normalised. Arbitrary; the display normalises to the Ly-alpha peak.
Quasar spectrum: 1 = the measured Selsing et al. 2016 composite (quasar_composite.csv); 0 = power law + emission_lines.csv (old hand-built template).

Typical redshift of the composite's own quasars (Selsing: 1 < z < 2.1; approximate). Used to divide out the average Ly-alpha forest already in the composite below 1216 Å so it is not absorbed twice. 0 = no correction.
Continuum slope below 912 Å: F_lambda ∝ lambda^-0.3 (alpha_nu = -1.7; Lusso et al. 2015). Joined continuously at 912 Å.
Helium is fully ionised below this z; above it everything shorter than 228 Å locally is absorbed.
Measured proximity-zone size at z ≈ 7 (transmission falls to 10%). Known z > 7 quasars: 1.3–1.9 pMpc.
tau(Ly-beta) / tau(Ly-alpha) = (f lambda)_beta / (f lambda)_alpha. Atomic constants.
Wavelength dependence of ionising opacity below 912 Å: (lambda / 912)^1.5.
How many absorbers to list for RedshiftMarks_NEW. [0] is always the first line.
Lowest absorber z listed for the marks. Just above the second cosmic web (z ≈ 0.8) so every mark exists when the demo points at them.
DESIGN DECISION: 1 = the piece shows Ly-alpha absorption only (lines born at 1216 Å and carried redward). 0 = all absorption. The flux grid always has the full physics.
Samples used to solve the absorption normalisation. More = steadier and slower.
Entries in the z(lookback) table the runtime uses.
Arrival frame (the zoom at Earth): left edge in EMITTED Å. 1000 = the classic forest figure (Q1422+2309).
Arrival frame: right edge in emitted Å. 1350 = the classic figure; shows the Ly-alpha peak and red continuum.
Samples in the arrival frame (log axis over journey bar + reference window). ~100 km/s. 64 KB in the file.
Samples of the quasar's emitted spectrum stored for the tutorial (log axis over every emitted wavelength the bar shows). 32 KB.
